facts.f: Three-toed sloths are among the slowest mammals on Earth.
facts.e: They often move less than a few metres in a minute.

facts.f: Giant sequoia trees in California are the largest trees by volume.
facts.e: The biggest one, called General Sherman, is thought to be over 2,000 years old.

facts.f: Coast redwoods are the tallest known trees.
facts.e: The tallest one ever measured is over 115 metres tall.

facts.f: Rafflesia arnoldii has the largest single flower in the world.
facts.e: It can be about a metre wide and smells like rotting meat to attract flies.

facts.f: Wolffia, also called watermeal, is the smallest flowering plant.
facts.e: Each plant is smaller than a grain of rice and floats on water.

facts.f: The bee hummingbird of Cuba is the smallest bird.
facts.e: It is only about 5 to 6 cm long.

facts.f: Elephants have the longest pregnancy of any land mammal: about 22 months.
facts.e: A baby elephant can weigh around 100 kg at birth.

facts.f: The Greenland shark may live longer than any other animal with a backbone.
facts.e: Scientists estimate that some may live for 250 years or more.

facts.f: The Great Wall of China is the longest wall ever built.
facts.e: Including all its branches, a 2012 survey measured it at about 21,000 km.

facts.f: When it opened in 2010, the Burj Khalifa in Dubai became the tallest building in the world.
facts.e: It is 828 metres tall.

facts.f: The Kumbh Mela is one of the largest peaceful gatherings of people on Earth.
facts.e: UNESCO added it to its list of Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2017.

facts.f: Some dung beetles can pull more than 1,000 times their own body weight.
facts.e: That makes them among the strongest animals for their size.

facts.f: The saltwater crocodile is the largest living reptile.
facts.e: Big males can grow to 6 metres long. They live in India's Sundarbans and Odisha's Bhitarkanika.

facts.f: The wandering albatross has the longest wingspan of any living bird.
facts.e: Its wings can stretch to about 3.5 metres from tip to tip.

facts.f: Bamboo is the largest member of the grass family.
facts.e: Some bamboos grow more than 30 metres tall.

facts.f: Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter, is the largest moon in the Solar System.
facts.e: It is even bigger than the planet Mercury.

facts.f: Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky.
facts.e: It is also called the Dog Star.

facts.f: Diamond is the hardest natural substance.
facts.e: It is so hard that it is usually scratched only by another diamond.

facts.f: Hydrogen is the most common element in the Universe.
facts.e: It is also the lightest element.

facts.f: Oxygen is the most common element in Earth's crust.
facts.e: It is joined with other elements in rocks and sand, such as silicon in quartz.

facts.f: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at normal room temperature.
facts.e: It was once used in thermometers.

facts.f: Silver is the best conductor of electricity of all metals.
facts.e: Copper is a close second and much cheaper, so it is used for most wires.

facts.f: The cricket ground at Chail in Himachal Pradesh is one of the highest in the world.
facts.e: It is about 2,444 metres above sea level.

facts.f: The coco de mer palm has the largest seed of any plant.
facts.e: One seed can weigh more than 15 kg. It grows in the Seychelles.

facts.f: Mercury is the fastest-moving planet.
facts.e: It zips around the Sun at about 47 km every second.

facts.f: Uranus has recorded the coldest temperatures of any planet, even though Neptune is farther away.
facts.e: Temperatures near −224 °C have been measured in its atmosphere.

facts.f: Titan, Saturn's largest moon, is the only moon with a thick atmosphere.
facts.e: It has lakes and rivers of liquid methane.

facts.f: The tiger is the largest member of the cat family.
facts.e: A big male Siberian tiger can weigh over 300 kg.

facts.f: Kangchenjunga is the highest mountain in India's Sikkim and the third-highest in the world.
facts.e: It has five peaks, and its name is often explained as 'five treasures of the snow'.

facts.f: Algeria is the largest country in Africa by area.
facts.e: Sudan was the largest until South Sudan became a separate country in 2011.

facts.f: Brazil is the largest country in South America.
facts.e: It covers nearly half of the continent.

facts.f: The cheetah can go from 0 to about 100 km per hour in about three seconds.
facts.e: That is faster than most sports cars.

facts.f: The blue whale's heart is the largest heart of any animal.
facts.e: It can weigh about 180 kg, as much as two or three grown-ups.

facts.f: The ostrich lays the largest egg of any living bird.
facts.e: One ostrich egg weighs about as much as 24 hen's eggs.

facts.f: The giraffe has the longest neck of any living animal, but only seven neck bones.
facts.e: Each neck bone can be over 25 cm long.

facts.f: The capybara of South America is the largest rodent in the world.
facts.e: It is a gentle, semi-aquatic animal that can weigh as much as an adult person.

facts.f: The Sahara is the largest hot desert, but Antarctica is the largest desert of all.
facts.e: A desert is defined by low rainfall, not by heat.

facts.f: The Pacific Ocean is larger than all the land on Earth put together.
facts.e: It covers about a third of Earth's surface.

facts.f: Jupiter has the shortest day of all the planets: about 10 hours.
facts.e: It spins faster than any other planet.

facts.f: Venus is the brightest planet in our sky.
facts.e: It is often seen shining brightly just after sunset or before sunrise.

facts.f: The goliath beetle is one of the heaviest insects in the world.
facts.e: Its larvae can weigh about 100 grams.

facts.f: The Indian Railways' Vivek Express runs one of the longest train routes in India.
facts.e: It travels from Dibrugarh in Assam to Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu, over 4,000 km.
